 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. TCU is closing in on adding Saint Louis transfer Robbie Avila two weeks into the 2026-27 college basketball season, On3's Joe Tipton confirms. Avila, the reigning Atlantic-10 Player of the Year, earned a preliminary injunction to play a fifth season from a St. Louis City Circuit Judge last week.
 This seemingly cleared the way for Avila to once again suit up for the Billikens this season. However, the College Sports Commission stepped in and blocked his route back to Saint Louis , as the program's roster was already at its 15-player limit. This ended his stint with the program.

 "The College Sports Commission has denied the request by Saint Louis University to add a 16th player to its 2026-27 men's basketball roster in violation of the roster limits imposed by the injunctions relief settlement in House v. NCAA," the statement read.
 This led to Avila evaluating other options, which now seems to be a stop in the Big 12. He'll join a TCU program that has opened the 2026-27 season with a 3-0 record. Under head coach Jamie Dixon , the Horned Frogs have reached the NCAA Tournament in four of the past five seasons.
 Robbie Avila to suit up for third different program
 Avila heads to Fort Worth with 1,990 career points, 750 career rebounds, and 473 career assists under his belt. He played his first two seasons of college basketball at Indiana State , and spent the past two at Saint Louis . Avila was named First Team All-MVC in 2024, Second Team All-Atlantic 10 in 2025, and First Team All-Atlantic 10 in 2026.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The Oak Forest, Ill. native went unselected in the NBA Draft, but signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Los Angeles Lakers. In August, the NCAA clarified that anyone who had signed an Exhibit 10 NBA contract would not be allowed back in college basketball. However, Avila very well seems like he could be on his way to doing so.
 If he does indeed end up suiting up for the Horned Frogs, it would mark the third different program that Avila will have played for. His team reached the NCAA Tournament in just one of his previous four seasons of play ( Saint Louis in 2026).
